0.heading: Your current site is losing you customers

1.heading: You're spending weeks on what should take days

2.heading: You can't afford to guess what works
2.description: You launched a page, got some traffic, and have no idea what happened next. No conversion data, no scroll depth, no way to know if the page is working or wasting your ad spend.

0.question: How long does it take to build a landing page?
0.answer: Most landing pages are live within 1-2 weeks from kickoff. We start with a design review, build in Next.js, optimize for performance, and deploy to Vercel.

1.question: Can I update the content myself after launch?
1.answer: Yes. We can integrate a headless CMS like Sanity or Contentful so you can edit text, images, and sections without touching code. Alternatively, we hand off the Git repository for developer-managed updates.

2.answer: Every landing page includes meta tags, Open Graph images, structured data (JSON-LD), sitemap generation, Core Web Vitals optimization, and semantic HTML. We also set up Google Search Console and analytics tracking.

wordpressMigration.title: WordPress → Next.js Migration
wordpressMigration.tagline: From slow to instant. In 1–2 weeks.
wordpressMigration.description: We migrate your WordPress site to a blazing-fast Next.js stack - AI-assisted, fixed price, with a 90+ PageSpeed guarantee. No plugin hell, no maintenance burden, just a site that works.

0.heading: Your WordPress site is costing you every day
0.description: Plugin subscriptions, managed hosting, developer bills for routine updates. Add it up and your WordPress site costs more per year than rebuilding it once in Next.js.

1.heading: Slow speed is killing your conversions
1.description: Run your own site through PageSpeed Insights. If you're on WordPress, you already know what the score looks like. Every second of load time costs you visitors who will never come back.

2.heading: Security patches are a full-time job
2.description: Another week, another plugin update. Another security advisory you're not sure applies to you. Static sites built in Next.js don't have a plugin layer to exploit.

0.question: Will I lose my SEO rankings during migration?
0.answer: No. We implement 1:1 URL mapping with proper 301 redirects, preserve all meta data, and maintain your sitemap structure. Most clients see rankings improve within weeks due to better performance signals.

1.question: Can I keep my WordPress content workflow?
1.answer: Yes. We can connect a headless CMS that feels similar to WordPress but serves content through Next.js. You keep the familiar editing experience with dramatically better frontend performance.

2.question: How long does a typical migration take?
2.answer: Simple brochure sites: 2-3 weeks. E-commerce or complex sites with custom plugins: 4-6 weeks. We run both sites in parallel during migration so there's zero downtime.

3.question: What happens to my WordPress plugins?
3.answer: We audit each plugin and replace them with modern equivalents. Contact forms become API routes, SEO plugins become built-in Next.js metadata, analytics move to PostHog or GA4, and caching becomes unnecessary with static generation.

4.question: What does the first week of a migration actually look like?
4.answer: Day one, we audit your existing site: pages, plugins, SEO structure, and hosting costs. By day three, you see a working prototype in Next.js with your content and branding. The rest of week one is refinement, redirect mapping, and performance benchmarking. You're involved at every step, but you don't have to manage the process.

0.answer: We assess your current systems, identify high-impact AI use cases, evaluate the right models and tools, and deliver an implementation roadmap. Depending on scope, this includes workshops with your team and a final presentation for stakeholders.

1.question: Do you also implement the recommendations?
1.answer: Yes. Many clients move directly into our AI & Automation service after consulting. The roadmap is designed to be actionable, whether we build it or your team does.

2.question: What AI experience backs this service?

3.answer: Starting with the technology instead of the problem. Teams pick a model or a framework, then look for something to do with it. The projects that work start with a specific, measurable pain point and work backward to the simplest solution that addresses it.

1.heading: Your runway is burning on the wrong things

0.question: What's included in the MVP scope?

1.question: Can I scale the MVP into a full product later?
1.answer: Absolutely. We build MVPs with production-grade architecture from day one - TypeScript, proper database schema, CI/CD, and monitoring. The codebase is designed to grow, not to be thrown away.

3.answer: We ask one question: does this feature help you learn something about your users? If the answer is no, it goes on the post-launch list. The goal of an MVP is to generate data, not to impress with feature count. Most founders are surprised by how little you need to start learning.

0.description: What worked for 100 users breaks at 10,000. Slow queries, timeout errors, and brittle integrations are signs you've outgrown your architecture.

0.question: What's your tech stack for full-stack applications?
0.answer: Next.js and React for the frontend, PostgreSQL with Drizzle ORM for the database, tRPC for type-safe APIs, Better Auth for authentication, and Vercel for deployment. We monitor with Sentry and PostHog.

1.question: Do you handle hosting and DevOps?

3.answer: It handles frontend, backend, and API routes in a single codebase. That means fewer moving parts, faster iteration, and one deployment pipeline instead of three. results.projectedHint: Estimated performance after we rebuild your site with Next.js
results.webVitalsSubtitle: These metrics directly affect how users experience your site and how Google ranks it.

vitalExplanations.FCP: First Contentful Paint - how quickly visitors see the first content. A slow FCP means users stare at a blank screen and are more likely to leave before your page even appears.
vitalExplanations.LCP: Largest Contentful Paint - when the main content becomes visible. If this takes longer than 2.5 seconds, roughly half of mobile visitors will leave before seeing your message.
vitalExplanations.TBT: Total Blocking Time - how long the page is unresponsive to clicks and taps. High blocking time means frustrated users who tap buttons and nothing happens.
vitalExplanations.CLS: Cumulative Layout Shift - how much the page layout jumps around while loading. Shifting content causes users to accidentally click the wrong thing, damaging trust.
vitalExplanations.SI: Speed Index - how quickly the visible area of your page is populated. A slow Speed Index means your site feels sluggish even if it eventually loads.
vitalExplanations.default: This metric affects how users perceive your site's speed and responsiveness.

intro.name: Sebastian Kehle
intro.tagline: Founder of webvise. AI Engineer at luca.
intro.description: Engineer at the intersection of design, full-stack development, and AI automation.

paragraphs.0: I studied visual communication and design in Berlin and spent my early career in agencies, building websites and campaigns that connected creative work with business outcomes. That foundation in design thinking still shapes every project at webvise.
paragraphs.1: In 2017, I took on the CEO role at a recruiting technology company, where I raised funding and led the team in designing and implementing the core matching algorithm. Running a startup taught me what it takes to ship fast under real constraints.
paragraphs.2: After that chapter, I founded webvise. What started as a design studio evolved into a full-stack practice delivering web applications, branding, and AI automation for businesses across the globe.
paragraphs.3: In 2021, I moved to the United States, launched a sold-out NFT collection on Solana, and co-founded Metagates, which later led to Abyss Online, a game that shipped on Steam. Building a product from concept to launch in a distributed international team sharpened my ability to ship under pressure and across time zones.
paragraphs.4: I joined luca, a Berlin-based hospitality platform serving thousands of restaurants and hotels across Germany. Starting as a Frontend Engineer shipping B2B features, I grew into the AI Engineer role, where I now build LLM-powered tools, internal automation pipelines, and intelligent systems. This hands-on AI engineering experience directly informs the AI solutions webvise delivers to clients.
paragraphs.5: In 2025, I collaborated with a team spanning Bangkok and Berlin to build an AI-powered game engine extension, further deepening my applied AI expertise. Today, webvise combines everything I have built across design, engineering, product, and AI into a practice that ships production software in weeks.
